nssf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Determines Allowed NSSAI
  • Assists AMF in slice selection during registration
  • UE sends Requested NSSAI → AMF asks NSSF → NSSF returns Allowed NSSAI
  • NSSF can determine AMF set serving the slice
  • Ensures correct slice allocation based on subscription and policies
  • Supports network slicing architecture in 5G
  • Maintains slice availability information
  • Enables efficient resource utilization across slices
  • Works indirectly with UDM and AMF for subscriber and slice data
  • Helps provide customized services (eMBB, URLLC, mMTC)
  • Improves scalability and service differentiation in 5G networks
amf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Handles UE registration and deregistration
  • Manages mobility management (handover, tracking area updates)
  • Receives and processes NAS signaling from UE
  • Coordinates authentication process with AUSF and UDM
  • Maintains UE context in the 5G Core
  • Assists in network slice selection (with NSSF)
  • Manages security context for user devices
  • Supports idle and connected mode transitions
  • Acts as the main control-plane interface between UE and 5G Core
udr:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Centralized data storage function in the 5G Core Network
  • Supports Service-Based Architecture (SBA) of 5G
  • Stores subscriber, policy, and application data
  • Enables data sharing across multiple network functions
  • Ensures secure and reliable data management
  • Critical for network slicing and personalization
  • Enhances network efficiency and performance
  • Supports real-time data updates
  • Uses RESTful APIs for data access
  • Works with UDM, PCF, NEF, and AUSF
  • Reduces data duplication across network elements
  • Improves network scalability and flexibility
smf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Session Establishment & Management
  • UE IP Address Allocation
  • DHCP Functions
  • Manages PDU session establishment, modification and release
  • Traffic Steering Configuration
  • Selects and controls the UPF for data routing
  • Enforces QoS policies for user sessions
  • Handles session continuity during mobility
  • Interacts with AMF for session-related signaling
  • Works with PCF to apply policy and charging rules
  • Supports network slicing by managing slice-specific sessions
  • Collects session-related charging information
  • Supports edge/MEC deployments for low latency
nef:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Enables secure exposure of network capabilities to external applications
  • Acts as a bridge between 5G Core and third-party services
  • Provides controlled access via APIs
  • Ensures authentication and authorization of external requests
  • Supports event exposure (location, QoS changes, congestion status
  • Enables application-driven QoS requests
  • Protects internal network functions from direct external access
  • Supports charging and policy control interactions
  • Facilitates IoT and enterprise application integration
  • Enhances service innovation in 5G ecosystems
nssaf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Performs slice-specific authentication and authorization
  • Ensures user access rights for a particular network slice
  • Enhances security in network slicing architecture
  • Works along with AUSF and AMF
  • Verifies subscription for slice-specific services
  • Prevents unauthorized access to dedicated slices
  • Supports enterprise and private network slicing
  • Strengthens isolation between multiple slices
  • Enables secure access to URLLC, eMBB, or mMTC slices
  • Improves reliability and trust in multi-slice deployments
pcf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Central policy decision function in 5G Core
  • Provides policy rules to SMF and AMF
  • Controls QoS (Quality of Service) parameters
  • Manages charging and billing policies
  • Supports network slicing policy control
  • Enables traffic prioritization and flow control
  • Interacts with UDR to retrieve policy data
  • Supports dynamic policy updates in real time
  • Applies subscriber-specific service policies
  • Works within the Service-Based Architecture (SBA)
  • Supports roaming policy management
  • Ensures efficient resource utilization across the network
scp:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Acts as an intermediary for NF-to-NF communication in 5G Core
  • Supports indirect communication in Service-Based Architecture (SBA)
  • Provides load balancing between network functions
  • Enables routing and forwarding of service requests
  • Enhances security with message screening and authorization
  • Supports network function discovery (via NRF integration)
  • Improves scalability in cloud-native deployments
  • Enables traffic monitoring and analytics
  • Supports resilience and failover mechanisms
  • Reduces direct dependencies between network functions
nrf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Acts as the service registry in 5G Core
  • Stores NF profiles and service capabilities
  • Enables NF discovery in Service-Based Architecture (SBA)
  • Supports dynamic registration and deregistration of NFs
  • Provides information for NF selection and service routing
  • Ensures efficient communication between network functions
  • Stores NF profiles and service capabilities
  • Enhances scalability in cloud-native 5G networks
  • Supports authorization of NF-to-NF communication
  • Critical for maintaining flexible and modular 5G architecture
af:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Represents external or internal application server in 5G
  • Interacts with the 5G Core via NEF
  • Requests specific QoS requirements for applications
  • Supports service-specific policy control
  • Provides application information to PCF
  • Enables real-time service optimization
  • Used in services like VoNR, IoT, OTT apps, gaming
  • Can trigger policy updates based on application needs
  • Supports network slicing awareness
  • Enhances user experience by aligning network behavior with app demands
ausf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Performs user authentication in 5G Core
  • Verifies subscriber identity during registration
  • Works closely with UDM for authentication data
  • Receives authentication request from AMF
  • Generates and validates authentication responses
  • Supports 5G-AKA and EAP-AKA’ authentication methods
  • Ensures secure access to network services
  • Protects against unauthorized network access
  • Part of the 5G control plane
  • Enhances subscriber privacy and security
upf:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Packet Routing & Forwarding
  • Anchor Point for Mobility
  • Traffic/Packet Inspection
  • QoS Handling and QoS enforcement
  • Traffic Usage Reporting
  • Uplink and downlink data transfer
  • User data handling
  • Session management support
  • Charging data generation
  • Packet filtering, mobility anchoring
  • Low-latency data processing
  • Support for network slicing
  • integration with edge/MEC computing
  • High-throughput user plane processing
udm:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Manages subscriber profile data in 5G Core
  • Handles authentication and authorization support
  • Works closely with AUSF for user authentication
  • Stores and manages subscription information
  • Supports mobility management data
  • Provides data to AMF, SMF, and PCF when required
  • Replaces HLR/HSS functions from 4G in 5G architecture
  • Supports network slicing subscription details
  • Ensures secure access to user-related data
  • Enables scalable and centralized data management
  • Supports Service-Based Architecture (SBA) in 5G
  • Plays a key role in maintaining user identity management
ue:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Acts as the end device that connects users to the 5G network
  • Initiates registration and authentication procedures with the network
  • Sends and receives user data and signaling messages
  • Establishes PDU sessions for data communication
  • Supports mobility management as the user moves between cells
  • Communicates with the gNodeB through the NR air interface
  • Enables access to services such as voice, data, IoT, and multimedia
  • Supports advanced features like high-speed data and low latency communication
  • Maintains subscriber identity using SIM/USIM credentials
  • Enables connectivity for a wide range of devices including smartphones, IoT devices, vehicles, and industrial equipment

📱 UE Types

  • Smartphones, IoT Devices, Tablets, Vehicles (V2X), AR/VR Devices, Industrial Equipment
ran:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Provides wireless connectivity between UE and the 5G network
  • Manages radio resource allocation and scheduling
  • Handles handover and mobility management between cells
  • Transmits and receives radio signals using the NR air interface
  • Forwards control-plane signaling to AMF via N2
  • Forwards user-plane data to UPF via N3
  • Supports advanced technologies such as Massive MIMO and beamforming
  • Maintains reliable communication within the coverage area
  • Supports high data rates and low latency communication
  • Enables connectivity for large numbers of devices in dense deployments

Key Components of 5G RAN

  • gNodeB (gNB) — 5G base station providing radio connectivity
  • Central Unit (CU) — Handles higher-layer protocols and control functions
  • Distributed Unit (DU) — Manages real-time radio processing and scheduling
  • Massive MIMO Antennas
  • Beamforming Capabilities
dn:
🎯 Key Responsibilities

  • Provides external connectivity for user applications and services
  • Acts as the destination network for user data traffic
  • Enables access to services such as the internet, cloud platforms, and enterprise networks
  • Receives and sends user data through the UPF via the N6 interface
  • Supports different types of networks including public internet and private enterprise networks
  • Allows network slices to connect to different service environments
  • Enables applications such as web services, streaming, VoIP, IoT platforms, and enterprise applications
  • Supports integration with cloud services and service provider platforms
